title: Chapter 41: The Stalk of Grass 9
content:
Chapter 41

The Stalk of Grass 9

The smile froze on Xiao Xingchen’s face.

The two words—Xue Yang—struck him like a physical blow. The faint color he had held completely vanished in an instant, leaving his lips a pale, bloodless shade of ash.

Almost unable to believe it, Xiao Xingchen whispered, “…Xue Yang?”

Suddenly breaking out of the daze, he demanded, “A-Qing, where did you hear that name?”

“Xue Yang is the guy living under our roof!” A-Qing blurted out. “It’s that piece of trash!”

Xiao Xingchen stood there, entirely lost. “The one with us? …The one living here? …”

He shook his head as if overcome by dizziness. “How do you know this?”

“I heard him kill someone!”

Xiao Xingchen pressed, “He killed someone? Who?”

“A woman!” A-Qing babbled, spinning the cover story she had spent all night refining. “Sounded young, carrying a sword. Xue Yang had a hidden blade too, and they started fighting—loud, hard strikes clashing everywhere. That girl screamed out his name, calling him ‘Xue Yang.’ She said he slaughtered whole temples, set fires, murdered people, and that he was a monster everyone had the right to hunt down! Heaven above, Daozhang, he’s a bloodthirsty psychopath! He’s been hiding right beside us all along, and god knows what he wants!”

A-Qing hadn't slept a wink, working on this lie the whole night. Above all else, she could never let Xiao Xingchen find out that he had slaughtered living human beings mistaking them for corpses—and, worst of all, that he had run Song Lan through with his own hands. Guilt tore at her for hiding Song Daozhang’s fate, but she had to swallow it. Her only goal was to get Xiao Xingchen to realize who Xue Yang was and run—pack up and flee as far away as humanly possible!

Yet the revelation was so horrifying, so utterly preposterous at first glance, that Xiao Xingchen simply couldn't wrap his mind around it. “That’s impossible. His voice doesn't match. And besides…”

Desperate, A-Qing jabbed her bamboo pole into the dirt. “He put on a fake voice on purpose! He was terrified you’d recognize him!” A sudden spark flashed in her mind, and she jumped up. “Wait, wait! His fingers! He’s only got nine fingers! Daozhang, didn't you know? Xue Yang has nine fingers, right? You must've seen it back then!”

Xiao Xingchen’s legs gave out under him.

A-Qing caught him in a hurry, steering him over to the table and easing him down onto a stool. A long silence hung in the room before Xiao Xingchen found his voice: “A-Qing… how would you know he only has nine fingers? Did you touch his hand? But if he truly were Xue Yang, how could he ever let you near his left hand, let alone allow you to discover his missing finger?”

A-Qing bit her lower lip, steeling herself. “…Daozhang! I'm coming clean! I’m not blind! I can see! I didn't touch it—I saw it with my own two eyes!”

Shock after shock struck like thunderclaps, leaving Xiao Xingchen bewildered. “What did you say? You can see?”

Terror gripped A-Qing’s chest, but the secret was out, and there was no turning back. She bowed her head, apologizing over and over: “I'm sorry, Daozhang, I didn't mean to lie to you! I was scared that if you knew I wasn't blind, you’d kick me out and leave me behind! But please, don't be mad at me right now—we have to run! He’s going to be back from buying groceries any second!”

Her voice cut off abruptly.

The bandages wrapped around Xiao Xingchen’s eyes had always been pure, stark white. But right then, two blooming stains of crimson began seeping outward from beneath the cloth. Slowly, steadily, the blood bled through the fabric, trickling down the hollows of his eye sockets.

A-Qing let out a terrified shriek. “Daozhang, you’re bleeding!”

Xiao Xingchen seemed to register it only after hearing her cry. He let out a faint, hollow gasp, reaching up to touch his face. His fingers came away slick with dark red. Trembling, A-Qing tried to dab at it with her sleeve, but the more she wiped, the faster it welled up. Xiao Xingchen held up a hand. “I’m fine… I’m fine.”

Long ago, excessive stress and emotional turmoil would reopen the wounds where his eyes had been gouged out. But the bleeding hadn't flared up in years, leading Wei Wuxian to believe the scars had fully settled. To see it erupt again today showed how devastating the shock truly was.

Xiao Xingchen mumbled, dazed, “But… if he’s really Xue Yang, why? Why didn't he just kill me from the start, instead of lingering at my side for all these years? How could it possibly be him…?”

“Because he couldn't do it right away!” A-Qing blurted out. “I saw the look in his eyes back then—he looked vicious, terrifying! But he was grievously wounded and couldn't move; he needed someone to nurse him back to health! I didn't know who he was, but if I’d known he was that butcher, I would've driven my bamboo pole straight through his throat while he was lying in the grass! Daozhang, let's just run, please?!”

Inside her memories, Wei Wuxian could only sigh. It’s too late. If she kept him in the dark, he’d go on living with a monster. But now that he knows, Xiao Xingchen isn't the type to just turn tail and run. He will demand an answer to his face. There is no good way out of this.

Sure enough, once Xiao Xingchen managed to steady his breathing, he said quietly, “A-Qing, you need to leave.”

His voice was hoarse. A-Qing stared at him, panic rising in her throat. “Me? Daozhang, we’re leaving together!”

Xiao Xingchen shook his head. “I cannot leave. I have to find out what he’s after. He wouldn't disguise himself and stay by my side for years without an objective. If I run and leave him loose here, the people remaining in Yi City will suffer at his hands. That is simply the kind of man Xue Yang is.”

This time, A-Qing broke down into genuine, frantic sobs. Tossing her bamboo cane aside, she clamped her arms around his legs. “Leave alone? How am I supposed to leave by myself, Daozhang?! I’m sticking with you! If you won't run, I won't either—at worst, he can just kill us both! I’d end up dying miserable and alone out there anyway! If you don't want that for me, you have to run with me!”

Unfortunately, now that the truth about her vision was out, playing the helpless, dependent card no longer worked. Xiao Xingchen said softly, “A-Qing, you have your sight, and you are clever. I know you can make a good life for yourself out there. You have no idea how terrifying a person Xue Yang is. You cannot stay, and you must never go near him again.”

The scream trapped inside A-Qing’s chest echoed so loudly that even Wei Wuxian felt it: I know! I know better than anyone how monstrous he is!

Yet she couldn't bring herself to utter the full, bloody truth.

Light, breezy footsteps echoed from down the road.

Xue Yang was back.

Xiao Xingchen snapped his head toward the door, every instinct of a seasoned cultivator snapping instantly into place. Hauling A-Qing close, he commanded in a harsh whisper, “When he steps inside, I’ll engage him. Take that split second and run. Hear me?”

Dumb with terror, A-Qing nodded frantically through her tears. A dull thud shook the door as Xue Yang gave it a kick from outside. “What are you two doing in there? I’m already back, and you still haven't left? If you’re inside, unbolt the door and let me in. I’m dead tired.”

Going by the bright, carefree tone alone, one would think it was just a playful junior disciple from next door. Who could ever guess that the creature standing beyond the wood was an unhinged demon dressed in a handsome human shell, walking on two legs and mimicking human speech?

The door wasn't locked, only barred from the inside. Any delay in opening it would set off Xue Yang’s alarms, and he’d step in with his guard up. Wiping the tears off her cheeks, A-Qing spat out, “Tired my ass! How far is the market, anyway—take two steps and you’re wiped out?! Big deal if I took my sweet time picking out an outfit, did it cost you a limb?!”

Xue Yang snorted in disdain. “You own, what, two shirts? Change all you want, you look identical. Open up, open up.”

A-Qing’s knees knocked together, but she kept her voice razor-sharp: “Tch! Not a chance! Kick it down if you're so tough!”

Xue Yang chuckled. “You said it, not me. Daozhang, you better fix the door frame later—don't blame me.”

With a casual kick, he shattered the latch. Stepping smoothly over the high wooden threshold, he sauntered in, one hand hoisting a basket overflowing with greens, radishes, and buns, the other clutching a bright red apple. He had just snapped off a crisp bite when he glanced down.

The silver point of Shuanghua was buried deep in his abdomen.

The woven basket slipped from his grip, sending radishes, greens, apples, and steamed buns tumbling across the dirt floor.

Xiao Xingchen barked, “A-Qing, run!”

A-Qing bolted, tearing out the front entrance of the funeral home. She sprinted down the road for several yards, then veered sharply, circling quietly back around the building. Scrambling up to her familiar spying perch, she poked her head out just enough to peer inside.

Xiao Xingchen’s voice was venomously cold: “Fun, was it?”

Xue Yang took another slow, deliberate bite of the apple in his hand. He chewed unhurriedly, swallowed, and let a crooked grin spread. “Fun. Why wouldn't it be?”

He was using his real voice now—low, smooth, and sharp.

Xiao Xingchen asked, “All these years at my side… what were you after?”

Xue Yang shrugged. “Who knows. Boredom, maybe.”

Xiao Xingchen ripped Shuanghua free, drawing the blade back for another lethal thrust. Xue Yang spoke up smoothly: “Daozhang Xiao Xingchen, remember that story I didn't finish? Don't tell me you aren't curious about the ending.”

“I’m not,” Xiao Xingchen said flatly.

Despite the rejection, his head tilted ever so slightly, the momentum of his sword hanging suspended in the air.

“Well, I'm telling it anyway,” Xue Yang said, his eyes glittering. “Hear it out. If you still think I’m in the wrong afterward, you can do whatever you like with me.”

He casually pressed a hand against the puncture wound in his belly to stem the blood, speaking without a trace of hurry: “That little kid, after taking that beating, ran into the man who tricked him into delivering the letter. He was miserable, but he was relieved, too. Bawling his eyes out, he threw himself forward and told him: the letter was delivered, but the sweets were gone, and he’d been beaten bloody. Could the man please just give him another plate?

“Now, that coward had clearly just been cornered by the brute and thrashed within an inch of his life. He was covered in bruises. Seeing a filthy beggar boy clinging to his leg set him off, and he kicked the child away in disgust.

“He climbed into an ox cart and ordered the driver to whip the beasts into a run. The kid scrambled to his feet, chasing after the cart for all he was worth. He wanted that plate of sweet pastries so badly. He actually caught up, waving his tiny hands in front of the wheels, begging them to stop. Irritated by the racket, the man snatched the whip from the driver's grip and lashed it across the kid's skull, dropping him flat on the road.”

Xue Yang paused, enunciating every syllable: “And then… the heavy wooden wheel rolled right over the boy’s hand. Bone by bone. Finger by finger.”

Blind or not, Xue Yang raised his left hand toward Xiao Xingchen. “Seven years old! Every single bone in that left hand crushed to powder, one finger mangled into bloody mush on the spot! And that man in the cart was Chang Ping’s father.

“Daozhang Xiao Xingchen, when you dragged me before the sect leaders at Jinlintai, weren't you so wonderfully righteous? Denouncing me for wiping out an entire clan over a ‘petty grudge.’ Tell me, is it because those fingers weren't attached to your body that you couldn't fathom the agony? Is it because you’ve never heard a scream that tore your own throat to shreds?! You ask why I had to butcher his entire bloodline? Why didn't you ask him why he felt the urge to toy with a starving child just to pass the time?! The Xue Yang standing before you was carved by Chang Ci’an’s own hand! The Chang Clan of Yueyang merely reaped what they sowed!”

Xiao Xingchen reeled in pure disbelief. “Chang Ci’an broke one of your fingers. Even if you wanted retribution, you could have severed one of his! If the hatred ran that deep, take two! Take ten! Take his entire arm! Why did you have to butcher his whole family?! Does one finger of yours demand the blood of more than fifty innocent lives?!”

Xue Yang appeared to give it genuine thought, as though the question itself were absurd. “Of course it does. The finger was mine; their lives belonged to someone else. You could stack a mountain of them and it still wouldn't balance the scales. What’s fifty-something people compared to one of my fingers?”

Sickened by his sheer, unapologetic arrogance, Xiao Xingchen’s face grew even paler. “Then what about the others?! Why butcher the disciples of Baixue Temple?! Why tear out Daozhang Song Zichen’s eyes?!”

Xue Yang sneered back, “Then why did you get in my way?! Why did you have to meddle in my business?! Why stick your neck out for that piece-of-shit Chang family?! Were you saving Chang Ci’an, or were you saving Chang Ping? Hahahaha! Remember how Chang Ping cried tears of gratitude at first? And remember how he later fell to his knees, begging you never to help him again? Daozhang Xiao Xingchen, you were in the wrong from the very beginning. You had no business sticking your nose into other people’s grudges! Right and wrong, debts and grievances—who the hell are you to judge? Or better yet, you never should have walked down that mountain in the first place! Your master, Baoshan Sanren, was the smart one. Why didn't you listen to her and stay tucked away playing immortal? If you don't understand how the mortal world works, don't set foot in it!”

Pushed past his limit, Xiao Xingchen choked out, “…Xue Yang, you are… truly sickening…”

At those words, the feral, predatory glint that had remained hidden for years flashed back into Xue Yang’s gaze.

He let out a low, venomous laugh. “Xiao Xingchen, that right there is exactly why I despise you. The people I loathe most in this world are self-righteous hypocrites like you—paragons of virtue who think a handful of good deeds will make the world a better place. You idiot. You naive, brainless fool! You find me sickening? Great. You think I give a damn about being called disgusting? But tell me… do you really have the right to look down on me?”

Xiao Xingchen faltered slightly. “What do you mean?”

Outside, both A-Qing and Wei Wuxian felt their hearts slam against their ribs.

Xue Yang’s tone shifted, sickeningly sweet. “We haven't been out hunting corpses much lately, have we? But these past couple of years… didn't we go out every few nights to slaughter a whole bunch?”

Xiao Xingchen’s lips twitched, a sudden, cold dread prickling down his spine. “Why are you bringing that up now?”

“No reason,” Xue Yang purred. “Just such a pity you're blind. Carved your own eyeballs out and gave them away, so you couldn't see the look on those ‘walking corpses’ faces when your sword skewered their hearts. How terrified they were. How agonizing it was. Some of them even dropped to their knees, weeping and knocking their heads against the dirt, begging you to spare their families. If I hadn't sliced their tongues out beforehand, they would have been screaming bloody murder: ‘Daozhang, have mercy!’”

Xiao Xingchen began to shake uncontrollably.

It took agonizing seconds for him to force out a hoarse rasp: “You’re lying. You’re trying to trick me.”

“Sure, I'm lying,” Xue Yang chuckled. “I’ve been lying to you every single day. Who knew you’d buy all the bullshit, but choke on the one truth I actually handed you?”

Xiao Xingchen stumbled forward, hacking his sword through the air with blind fury. “Shut up! Shut up!”

Clutching his bleeding stomach, Xue Yang snapped his fingers with his left hand, stepping back with fluid grace. The expression on his face was stripped of anything remotely human. A sickly green hue flickered in his dark eyes, and the canine teeth showing through his wide grin made him look like a demon fresh out of hell. He jeered, “Fine! I’ll shut my mouth! If you don't believe me, why don't you cross blades with the creature behind you? Let him tell you whether I'm lying or not!”

A rush of sword wind sliced from behind. By reflex, Xiao Xingchen whipped Shuanghua around in a clean parry.

The moment steel met steel, he froze.

Not merely froze—his entire being seemed to petrify into an empty, hollow husk of stone.

Xiao Xingchen asked, his voice terribly soft, terribly fragile: “…Is that you, Zichen?”

There was no answer.

The corpse of Song Lan stood before him, white-eyed and hollow, staring forward with unseeing eyes as the blades remained locked together.

In years past, the two must have sparred thousands of times. A single clash of steel, the specific weight and flow of spiritual energy, was all it took to recognize each other. Yet Xiao Xingchen refused to believe it. Trembling, he turned slowly, reaching out a shivering hand until his bare fingers brushed the cold steel of Song Lan’s sword.

The fierce corpse did not move. Xiao Xingchen’s hand traced up the blade until his fingers mapped out the two characters carved into the hilt: Fuxue.

Every drop of color drained from Xiao Xingchen’s face.

His fingers clawed blindly at Fuxue’s edge, not even noticing as the razor-sharp steel bit deep into his palm, slicing it open. His entire frame shook so violently his words scattered into broken sobs: “…Zichen… Daozhang Song… Daozhang Song… is that you…?”

Song Lan looked down at him in total silence, mute and still.

The bandages over Xiao Xingchen’s eyes had turned into two grotesque craters of fresh, streaming blood. He reached out to touch the man holding the blade, but jerked his hands back in sheer horror, extending them only to retreat again. The tearing agony ripping through A-Qing’s chest made it hard for both her and Wei Wuxian to draw breath, tears streaming uncontrollably down her face.

Xiao Xingchen stood frozen, utterly destroyed. “…What happened…? Say something…”

His composure shattered entirely into a raw scream: “Someone say something?!”

Obliging his request, Xue Yang’s mocking voice chimed in: “Need me to spell out who that walking corpse was that you ran through yesterday?”

Clang.

Shuanghua slipped from Xiao Xingchen’s fingers, clattering against the stone floor.

Xue Yang burst into hysterical laughter.

Dropping to his knees before Song Lan’s towering, unresponsive corpse, Xiao Xingchen grabbed his own head and began to wail, a sound of pure, gut-wrenching despair.

Tears of laughter pricked the corners of Xue Yang’s eyes as he sneered, “Look at that! Two best friends reunited, weeping with joy! Why don't you give him a hug, huh?!”

A-Qing clamped both hands over her mouth, muffling her sobs so completely that not a single whimper slipped out. Inside the hall, Xue Yang paced back and forth, spewing curses in a tone oscillating madly between raw fury and psychotic euphoria: “Save the world?! God, what a joke! You couldn't even save yourself!”

A sharp, stabbing ache flared through Wei Wuxian’s skull—this time, it didn't belong to A-Qing’s spirit.

Curled at Song Lan’s feet, Xiao Xingchen looked shrunken, pathetic, reduced to a fragile, broken heap wishing he could simply cease to exist. His once-immaculate white robes were drenched in blood and caked in dirt. Xue Yang spat down at him, “You accomplished nothing! A total, pathetic failure! You brought every single bit of this on your own head!”

In that broken figure, Wei Wuxian saw a mirror of himself.

A total failure, covered in gore, achieving nothing, drowning in the accusations and screams of the world, helpless to turn back time, left with nothing but agonizing tears!

The bandages were saturated with red. With no eyes left in his sockets, Xiao Xingchen couldn't shed tears—only blood. Deceived for years, treating his sworn enemy like a companion, having his kindness stomped into the dirt, thinking he was cleansing the world of evil while his hands dripped with innocent lives… only to butcher his own soulmate with his own blade!

He could only choke out a ragged, broken plea: “Spare me… please, just let me go…”

Xue Yang mocked, “Weren't you trying to run me through a minute ago? Now you’re begging for mercy?”

He knew full well that with Song Lan’s fierce corpse standing guard, Xiao Xingchen would never have the strength to lift a sword again.

Xue Yang had won. A flawless, total victory.

Without warning, Xiao Xingchen lunged forward, snatching Shuanghua from the ground. Reversing the grip, he brought the razor edge up against his own throat. A pristine flash of silver sliced across Xue Yang’s dark, fathomless eyes. Xiao Xingchen let go, and a ribbon of crimson welled up, spilling down the frosty blade.

With the clean, ringing crash of the sword striking the pavement, Xue Yang’s laughter died in his throat.

A suffocating silence descended over the room. Slowly, he approached Xiao Xingchen’s motionless body, looking down. The twisted smirk on his face gradually slackened, fine red veins spidering through the whites of his eyes. If one looked closely, the rims of his eyes appeared faintly, impossibly red.

A second later, he bared his teeth, hissing through clenched jaws: “You forced my hand!”

With a frigid sneer, he muttered to himself, “Dead is better anyway! Dead things actually listen.”

He pressed two fingers to Xiao Xingchen’s neck, checking for a pulse, then squeezed his wrist, almost dissatisfied with how warm and supple the body still was. Turning on his heel, he walked into the back room and returned carrying a basin of clean water and a fresh cloth. Carefully, methodically, he wiped every smear of blood from the pale face, producing a clean strip of cloth to wrap tenderly around the empty sockets.

Dipping a finger in blood, he mapped out an intricate array on the stone floor, arranging the necessary ritual components before lifting Xiao Xingchen’s body and placing it gently at the center. Only after finishing all of this did he finally remember to bind the gaping wound on his own abdomen.

Convinced that they would be speaking again within moments, his mood visibly brightened. He picked up the scattered groceries, neatly stacking the cabbages, radishes, and apples back into the wicker basket. In a rare burst of domesticity, he swept the entire room clean and lined the coffin where A-Qing slept with a fresh, thick blanket of dry straw. Finally, he pulled the candy Xiao Xingchen had given him the night before from his sleeve.

He brought it to his lips, hesitated, and tucked it back away. Sitting at the table with his chin resting in his palm, he waited, wholly bored, for Xiao Xingchen to sit back up.

Xiao Xingchen never moved.

As dusk deepened into shadows, Xue Yang’s expression turned increasingly sullen. His fingers drummed an irritated cadence against the wooden tabletop.

When night fell completely, he kicked the table, letting loose a foul curse. Hitching up his robes, he dropped to his knees beside the corpse to inspect the array and talismanic script. Everything looked correct. Frowning, he wiped the entire array away and drew it from scratch.

This time, Xue Yang sat flat on the cold floor, staring unblinkingly at Xiao Xingchen with infinite patience. Up in her crawlspace, A-Qing’s legs had gone numb three times over, throbbing with an agonizing itch like thousands of ants burrowing through her flesh. Her eyes were swollen shut from crying, blurring everything into hazy smears.

Another two hours dragged by before Xue Yang finally realized something had gone catastrophically wrong.

He pressed his palm against Xiao Xingchen’s forehead, closing his eyes to search the spiritual veins. A beat later, his eyes snapped open in horror.

Wei Wuxian knew what he had found: nothing more than a few faint, shattered embers of a soul.

A spirit fractured to this degree was impossible to forge into a fierce corpse.

It was as if Xue Yang had never once accounted for this possibility. For the very first time, the wicked grin permanently etched into his face vanished, replaced by an absolute, terrifying blankness.

Panicking on raw instinct, he clamped both hands over the wound on Xiao Xingchen’s throat. But the blood had run cold hours ago. The flesh was paper-white, and thick, rust-brown crusts clung to the dead skin. Clamping the cut now was entirely useless.

Xiao Xingchen was dead. Dead down to the marrow.

Even his soul had shattered into dust.

In Xue Yang’s childhood story, the starving boy wailing over a missed treat seemed worlds apart from the psychotic monster he had become. Yet in this single moment, Wei Wuxian finally caught a glimpse of that terrified, helpless child staring back through the killer's eyes.

Blood vessels burst across Xue Yang’s sclera. Bolting upright with balled fists, he went berserk, rampaging through the funeral home. He shattered furniture, hurled pots, and tore through the space in a frenzy of violent crashes, reducing the room he had just meticulously tidied to splinters.

The snarls ripping from his chest were more feral and insane than anything he had displayed before.

Once the storm of destruction burned out, an eerie quiet settled over him. He sank back onto his haunches beside the body, whispering softly: “Xiao Xingchen.”

He coaxed, “If you don't get up, I’m going to order your dear friend Song Lan to go slaughter people.

“I’ll slaughter every living soul in Yi City and turn them into puppets. You lived here for so long—can you really afford to ignore them?

“I’ll choke that little blind brat A-Qing to death with my bare hands. I’ll dump her corpse in the wild and let stray dogs tear her into scraps.”

Above, A-Qing shuddered in utter terror.

No response came. Xue Yang’s voice detonated into an enraged bellow: “Xiao Xingchen?!”

Desperate, he seized the collar of the white Daoist robes, shaking the lifeless shell, glaring down into the unmoving face.

Suddenly, he scooped Xiao Xingchen’s body up, hoisting the dead weight onto his back.

Stumbling out the door like a madman, Xue Yang muttered under his breath in a frantic loop: “A spirit-trapping pouch… a spirit-trapping pouch. Right, a spirit-trapping pouch! I need a spirit-trapping pouch, spirit-trapping pouch, spirit-trapping pouch…”

Only after he had faded far into the mist did A-Qing dare to stir.

Her numb legs failed her, sending her tumbling from the crawlspace onto the floor. She wriggled like a worm for several minutes before dragging herself upright. Shuffling forward stiffly, she got the blood flowing through her veins again. Her steps grew faster, wilder, until she broke into a desperate sprint.

Only when Yi City had been left miles behind did she finally release the agonized wail trapped in her chest: “Daozhang! Daozhang! Waaah! Daozhang…!”

The vision shifted, jumping ahead to another place and time.

Some time had passed. A-Qing was wandering through an unfamiliar town, tapping her cane and playing the blind girl once more. Whenever someone crossed her path, she’d ask: “Excuse me, are there any great cultivation clans nearby?” “Sir, is there an immortal master nearby? A really powerful cultivator?”

Wei Wuxian understood: She was searching for someone powerful enough to avenge Xiao Xingchen.

Unfortunately, no one took a ragged blind girl seriously. People brushed her off with half-hearted answers and walked away. Undeterred, A-Qing kept asking, over and over, enduring the waves of hands shoving her aside. Finding nothing, she turned down a narrow dirt trail leading into the hills.

Exhausted after a full day on her feet, she dragged her heavy limbs over to a trickling stream. Cupping the cold water to her lips, she drank deeply, cooling her parched throat. Glancing at her reflection, she caught sight of the wooden hairpin tucked into her hair, reaching up to gently draw it out.

It had originally been a crude, uneven twig, like a lumpy chopstick. Xiao Xingchen had shaved it smooth and slender, carving a tiny fox at the tip. The fox had a sharp little muzzle, wide eyes, and a sweet, resting smile. The day she received it, she had run her fingers over the carving, beaming: “Look! It looks just like me!”

Staring down at the pin, A-Qing’s chin trembled, threatening tears. Her stomach growled violently. Digging into her robes, she pulled out a small white pouch—the one she had stolen from Xiao Xingchen years ago. Working her fingers inside, she extracted a single piece of candy. She gave it a cautious lick, letting the faint sweetness wash over her tongue, before tucking it carefully back into the pouch.

It was the very last piece of candy Xiao Xingchen had ever left for her.

Just as she pocketed the pouch, her eyes swept across the water’s surface. A second reflection had appeared behind her own.

Xue Yang was staring up from the ripple, smiling right at her.

A-Qing shrieked, scrambling back in sheer panic.

No one knew how long he had been standing there. Holding Shuanghua, Xue Yang spread his arms in an inviting embrace, his voice dripping with cheerful warmth: “A-Qing, why run? It’s been so long—didn't you miss me?”

A-Qing screamed at the top of her lungs: “Help! Somebody help me!”

Yet they were stranded on a deserted mountain path; no savior was going to appear.

Xue Yang arched an eyebrow. “I just finished up some business in Yueyang and was heading back, only to catch you asking around town. Truly, what an inescapable twist of fate. Then again, I have to give you credit—you played the blind act so well you fooled even me for years. Impressive.”

A-Qing knew her time was up. There was no running, no surviving. Once the initial wave of horror passed, a fierce recklessness took hold: if she was going to die anyway, she might as well tear him a new one before she went. Springing to her feet, she spat: “You ungrateful beast! You filthy, rotten mongrel! Did your parents conceive you in a pigsty to birth a bastard like you?! You worthless piece of shit raised on sewage!”

Growing up on the rough streets, she had heard every foul curse in the book, and now she spewed them all like venom.

Xue Yang listened with an amused grin. “Quite the mouth on you. How come I never heard you swear like this in front of Xiao Xingchen? Got anything else?”

A-Qing snarled, “Shut your shameless mouth! How dare you speak his name! That’s his sword—you think you’re worthy of touching it?! You're polluting his steel!”

Lifting Shuanghua in his left hand, Xue Yang admired the frosty edge. “Oh, this? It’s mine now. Did you really think your precious Daozhang was so clean? Soon enough, he’ll belong to me, too…”

“Bullshit! Keep dreaming!” A-Qing snapped, cutting him off. “You don't get to judge how pure he was! You're nothing but a gob of spit! He had eight lifetimes of bad luck just to get stepped on by you! The only filthy thing here is you—a disgusting clump of phlegm!”

The smirk finally dropped from Xue Yang’s face.

Having fled in terror for so long, finally facing the end brought a strange, sudden calm to A-Qing’s chest.

Xue Yang’s voice turned dangerously soft: “Since you love playing blind so much… why don't you become a real one?”

With a flick of his wrist, a cloud of blinding powder caught her full in the face, burning straight into her open eyes. Her vision flashed searing crimson, then plunged into absolute black.

Agony tore through her eyeballs, and A-Qing screamed in torment. Xue Yang’s voice drifted over the dark: “Such a loud mouth. No need to keep that tongue of yours, either.”

Something icy and sharp plunged straight into her mouth. Wei Wuxian barely felt the searing puncture at the root of her tongue before an invisible force violently yanked him back.

Ting… ting…

The crisp, clear chime of a silver bell rang inches from his ears. Still drowning in A-Qing’s agony, Wei Wuxian’s senses spun, the world tilting precariously on its axis. Lan Jingyi waved a frantic hand in front of his face. “No reaction?! Don't tell me he went stupid?!”

Jin Ling scolded, “I warned you, Empathy is dangerous!”

“It’s your fault for spacing out and not ringing the bell on time!” Lan Jingyi snapped back.

Jin Ling stiffened. “I…”

Fortunately, Wei Wuxian caught his breath, grabbing the edge of the coffin to haul himself upright. A-Qing’s spirit had detached from his form, hovering nearby and clinging to the wooden planks. The juniors swarmed forward like a litter of startled piglets, clamoring all at once: “He’s up! He’s up!” “Thank goodness, he’s not braindead!” “Wasn't he already a little touched in the head?” “Shut up, you idiot!”

With the chatter buzzing in his ears, Wei Wuxian pressed a hand to his temple. “Keep it down, my head is pounding.”

The boys fell silent instantly. Reaching down into the coffin, Wei Wuxian carefully parted the clean collar of Xiao Xingchen’s robes. Sure enough, right across the throat lay a thin, fatal scar.

Wei Wuxian’s heart sank with profound grief. Looking at A-Qing, he murmured softly, “You went through hell.”

The reason her ghost was blind, yet moved without the hesitant fumbling of the sightless, was that she had only lost her eyes in the final moments of her life. Before that horrific day, she had always been a nimble, spirited girl who sprinted like the wind.

To spend years lurking alone within the haunted fog of Yi City, playing ghost to spite Xue Yang, scaring away living travelers to save them from slaughter, pointing them toward safety… the sheer courage and raw obsession that took was beyond measure.

Clinging to the coffin, A-Qing pressed her hands together, bowing repeatedly to Wei Wuxian. She then brandished her bamboo cane like a blade, miming her old, familiar stabbing motions.

Wei Wuxian said quietly, “Rest easy.”

Turning to the boys, he commanded, “Stay put here. The walking corpses in town won't dare approach this funeral hall. I’ll be back shortly.”

Lan Jingyi couldn't hold back. “What on earth did you see in there?!”

Wei Wuxian replied, “Too long to tell now. I’ll explain later.”

Jin Ling pressed, “Can't you give us the short version? Don't leave us hanging!”

Wei Wuxian looked back over his shoulder. “Short version: Xue Yang dies today.”

Through the blinding demonic fog, A-Qing’s bamboo pole tapped a frantic rhythm, leading the way. Cultivator and spirit moved like wind, swiftly returning to the chaotic battlefield.

Lan Wangji and Xue Yang had taken the clash outside, where the glares of Bichen and Jiangzai crossed in a ferocious duel. Bichen was calm, precise, and steadily dominating the field, while Jiangzai snapped and slashed like a rabid hound, barely holding the line. Yet the dense fog was blinding, hampering Lan Wangji’s sight, whereas Xue Yang had stalked Yi City for years; like A-Qing, he could map every alley blindfolded, keeping the fight deadlocked. From time to time, the guqin roared through the mist, shockwaves scattering the encroaching hordes of walking corpses.

The moment Wei Wuxian drew his bamboo flute, two massive dark figures crashed to the cobblestones before him like collapsing iron towers. Wen Ning had Song Lan pinned to the ground, both fierce corpses locking their hands around each other's throats, bone grinding audibly against bone.

Wei Wuxian barked, “Hold him down!”

Dropping low, he ran his fingers through Song Lan’s hair, quickly catching the ends of the two skull-piercing nails. A wave of relief washed over him: these nails were far thinner than the ones once driven into Wen Ning, forged from entirely different materials. Restoring Song Lan’s consciousness wouldn't be impossible. Pincer-gripping the exposed ends, he worked them out slowly.

As the foreign iron was drawn from his skull, Song Lan’s eyes snapped wide open, a guttural rasp tearing from his throat. Wen Ning bore down with crushing force, keeping the thrashing corpse pinned. The second the nails came free, Song Lan went limp like a marionette with its strings cut, collapsing motionless against the dirt.

Just then, a roar of unhinged fury tore through the mist:

“Give it back to me!”
